title: BA6/2/2016 of Imran Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
B.A.6 No. 02 of 2016
U.C. Dhyani, J. Mr. Harendra Belwal and Mr. D.N. Sharma,
Advocates for the applicant.
Mr. K.S. Rawal, Brief Holder for the
respondent State.
 This is sixth bail application moved on behalf
of applicant Imran, who is in jail in connection with
case crime no. 37 of 2014 (S.T. no. 72 of 2012),
under Sections 302, 120B, registered at Police
Station, Patel Nagar, District Dehradun.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the documents brought on record.
Earlier all the bail applications were
dismissed by this Court on one pretext or another,
including on merits. While disposing of fifth bail
application liberty was granted to the applicant to
move an application under Section 437(7) Cr.P.C.
for applicant's release on bail.
Applicant tried, but failed again.
The complaint of learned counsel for the
applicant is that only 8 witnesses have been
examined so far and 32 others are yet to be
examined.
Any trial has to proceed in accordance with
law and the court below can only be given a
direction to make an endeavour to dispose of the
case of under trial at an early date. No time limit,
however, can be fixed.
This Court is not inclined to grant bail to the
applicant on the sole new ground that 8 witnesses
have been examined and 32 others remain to be
examined. There is no merit in the sixth bail
application. The same is, accordingly, dismissed.
